# Session Template

Every session runs the same five blocks in the same order, the way a practice does. The
sequence does not change week to week. What changes is the content inside each block.

| Block | Minutes | Clock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Announcements | 5 | 12:30 | Logistics, deadlines, program news |
| Quote of the Day and Leader Profile | 5 | 12:35 | One quote, one leader, briefly |
| Leadership Principle | 10 | 12:40 | The week's concept, taught |
| Drills | 10 | 12:50 | Follow along and build it live, usually with AI |
| Practice | 45 | 1:00 | Work session. Students build, coaches roam |

The first four blocks are the 30 minute leadership development block. Practice is the 45
minute working block, published on the schedule as the project roundtable.

## Announcements (5 min)

Program logistics only. Anything that takes longer than a minute to explain belongs in
Practice or in email. Standing items:

- Upcoming club events and who owns them
- Deadlines landing this week or next
- Recruiting calendar changes
- New hires, role changes, vacancies

## Quote of the Day and Leader Profile (5 min)

One quote and one leader, together in five minutes. Keep the profile to three or four
sentences: who they are, the decision or moment worth knowing, what it cost them.

Rotate who presents. A student leader takes this block, signs up a week ahead, and picks
both the quote and the profile. The only constraint is that the pair should connect to the
week's principle.

## Leadership Principle (10 min)

One principle, taught. The operating model names three skill areas to draw from: influence,
conflict, and managing up. Guest speakers and case discussions fill this block too.

Ten minutes buys one idea, not three. State the principle, give one example of it working,
give one example of it failing, then move to Drills.

## Drills (10 min)

A follow-along. You are at the front with your screen up, everyone has a laptop open, and
the room builds the same thing at the same time. Nobody watches a demo. If a student's
screen is dark, the drill is not working.

The default format is an AI follow-along: you narrate the prompt, everyone types their own
version, and the interesting part is where the outputs differ. Ten minutes is enough for one
artifact, not a workflow. Pick something a leader would actually produce this week.

Candidates:

- Draft the recruiting email to a firm contact, then compare what six people got back
- Turn a messy set of event notes into a one page brief
- Build the agenda for a club presidency meeting from a two sentence description
- Take a plan someone wrote and have AI argue against it, then judge whether it was right
- Summarize a case or article into the three sentences you would say out loud

Rules that keep it a drill and not a lecture:

- Everyone types. You go slow enough that the slowest person keeps up.
- Same starting prompt for the room, so the differences are visible.
- Stop at ten minutes even if it is unfinished. Unfinished is fine, it makes the point.
- Two or three people read their output out loud before you move on.

If a follow-along needs more room, take the extra five minutes from Practice rather than
from the Principle block.

## Practice (45 min)

Students take the rest of the hour and actually do the work. The drill showed them the move
once. Practice is where they run it on their own club's real deliverable, at their own desk,
for forty five minutes.

Scott, Sarah, and Luke roam the room the whole time. Roaming is the instruction method here.
There is no front of the room during Practice.

What roaming looks like:

- Read over a shoulder before saying anything
- Ask what they are trying to do, not what they are doing
- Two minutes per student, then move. Come back around rather than camping.
- Carry patterns forward: if three people hit the same wall, stop the room and say so

Sarah and Luke have two modes and can pick per week:

- **In the room.** Roam alongside Scott, same job, three coaches covering thirty students.
- **Broken out.** Pull a subgroup into a side conversation: a club that needs focused help, a
  first-time VP who needs onboarding, a team with a deadline that week. Or run their own
  work while available to the room.

Decide the mode in prep, not on the fly, so the room knows who to look for.

Club and presidency updates and cross-team coordination still need a home. Either give them
the first ten minutes of Practice before students scatter, or fold the standing items into
Announcements. Pick one and keep it the same every week.

## Weekly Prep Checklist

- [ ] Announcements collected from club leaders by Thursday
- [ ] Quote and Leader Profile presenter confirmed
- [ ] Principle chosen, with one success example and one failure example
- [ ] Follow-along built and run once yourself, with the starting prompt written down
- [ ] Practice: what each club is working on, so roaming has a target
- [ ] Sarah and Luke's mode set for the week: roaming or broken out
